app.title: Cursio
app.subtitle: Use this device as a touchpad for your computer

gallery.title: Gallery
gallery.description: Photos and videos of your other machines. They stay where they are until you save one.
gallery.noPeer: No machine is sharing its gallery
gallery.noPeerHint: Another machine has to be connected and running a Cursio that has the gallery. On a phone, allow "Photos on your other devices".
gallery.copyVideo: Only a photo can be copied

call.title: Call
call.failed: The phone did not do that

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: Your phone's text messages, read and answered from here. They stay on the phone.
messages.noPhone: No phone is sharing its messages
messages.noPhoneHint: Open Cursio on the phone and allow "Text messages on your computer". The phone has to be connected.
messages.pickHint: Your phone's texts show here; replies go out from the phone.
messages.enterHint: Enter sends · Shift+Enter for a new line
messages.handedOver: Handed to the phone to send
messages.loadFailed: Could not read the phone's messages
messages.sendFailed: The phone did not send it
messages.callFailed: The phone did not place the call

node.notRunningTitle: The Cursio node is not running on this machine
node.notRunningBody: Nothing is shared until it runs. Start it here, or run `cursio mesh` in a terminal.
node.startRequested: Starting the node; this window follows it once it answers.
node.notRunningTitlePhone: Cursio is not running on this phone
node.notRunningBodyPhone: Other machines cannot reach this phone until it runs. Starting it keeps it running in the background, with a notification saying so.

window.staleTitle: This window is older than Cursio
window.staleBody: The window runs {window}, the node already runs {node}. Some pages may not load until the window is the same version.

stats.latencyHint: The slower of wire-to-injection and capture-to-send, over the last 30 s
stats.latencyTrend: Input latency p99 since this window opened
stats.problemsHint: What the node found wrong on this machine, each with its fix

problems.title: Problems
problems.noneHint: The node raises a problem here the moment it finds one.

update.title: Version
update.waitingFor: Switching when it is quiet — waiting because {reason}.
update.applyBody: The node stops and comes back as the new version; links reconnect in a few seconds. If it does not come up, this version is started again.
update.drift: The node runs {running}, but the install points at {current}; restart the node to switch.
update.noInstall: No versioned install on this machine
update.noInstallHint: Builds staged with `cargo xtask stage --install` appear here.
update.rollbackBody: The node stops, the previous version starts in its place, and links reconnect in a few seconds. If it does not come up, the current version is started again.
update.rollingBack: Rolling back to {version}; the node restarts.

palette.placeholder: Search machines, settings, contacts, messages, or type a number to call…
palette.toggleModule: Turn a module on or off
palette.title: Command palette
palette.description: Search pages, settings, machines and their actions, modules, a phone's conversations and the node's log; call or text a number.
palette.searchFailed: The log could not be read.
palette.pageStatus: What this machine shares, the peers it reaches and anything wrong with it.
palette.pageSettings: Start at login, the theme and the running node.
palette.logSearch: Words to find in the node's log…
palette.toggleLogs: show or hide the log from anywhere

modules.title: What this machine shares
modules.description: A module runs on a link only when both machines have it on.
modules.inputHint: Capture this machine's input and move the cursor across screen edges
modules.clipboardHint: Copy here, paste there — text, images and formatting
modules.audioHint: Each app's sound reaches peers as its own stream
modules.filesHint: Peers' disks appear under ~/Cursio, and theirs see yours
modules.usbHint: Lend this machine's USB devices to peers
modules.remoteScreenHint: Offer peers' windows to Discord, OBS and browser calls here
modules.screenHostHint: Answer peers asking for this machine's windows
modules.pinned: Saved, but a command-line flag overrides it until the node is started without that flag.
modules.appliedNote: Changes are written to {path} and take effect at once; links stay up.
modules.restartNeeded: Waiting for a restart to apply: {fields}
modules.restartPhone: They apply the next time Cursio starts on this phone, such as after a reboot.

streams.title: Playing here
streams.description: Sound from other machines, at the volume you want it on this one. The sender and other listeners are not affected.
streams.none: Nothing is playing from other machines
streams.noneHint: An app's sound shows up here while a peer sends it to this machine.
streams.microphonesDescription: Other machines' microphones, as inputs any app here can record from. The slider sets how loud each one comes in.
streams.noMicrophones: No other machine offers a microphone
streams.noMicrophonesHint: A peer's microphones show up here once it shares them.
streams.failed: The volume of {name} was not changed

phone.title: Finish setting up this phone
phone.description: Android stops background apps unless they are allowed to stay. Cursio needs these to keep the phone reachable.
phone.notificationsHint: Android shows a running background service as a notification; without it, the service is stopped.
phone.microphoneHint: Lets other machines use this phone's microphone.
phone.batteryHint: Keeps links up while the screen is off.
phone.notificationAccessHint: Shows this phone's notifications on the computer you are at, with their buttons and replies.
phone.callsHint: Answer, decline and place this phone's calls from a computer. Pair the phone with the computer over Bluetooth to talk through the computer's speakers and microphone.
phone.messagesHint: Read this phone's SMS conversations and send texts from your computer.
phone.galleryHint: Browse this phone's photos and videos from your computers, and save the ones you want there.
phone.nearbyHint: When Wi-Fi does not reach your computer, Cursio carries on over Bluetooth with a computer this phone is paired with.
phone.storage: This phone's files on your computer
phone.storageHint: Your computer shows this phone's storage as a folder, to open, copy and save files as if they were local. Android asks for "All files access".
phone.companionHint: Lets Android keep Cursio running and start it again whenever a computer paired over Bluetooth is near — even after the phone stops it.
phone.touchHint: A computer showing this screen can tap, swipe and type with its mouse and keyboard. Turn on “Cursio: control from a computer” in the accessibility list.
phone.autostartHint: This phone also stops apps that are not on its own Autostart list. Allow Cursio there; Android cannot tell the app whether you did.
phone.requestFailed: The system screen did not open

peers.title: Peers
peers.noneHint: Pair one from the Pair tab.

peer.overBluetoothHint: Connected over Bluetooth because the network does not reach it: everything but screens and large files works, more slowly.
peer.skippedLacks: Not running with {peer}: it is switched off there, or {peer} runs an older Cursio — update it
peer.skippedVersion: Not running with {peer}: the two builds differ — update the older one
peer.noLink: Not connected in this session, so its position and status are unknown.

peerMenu.screenAsked: Asked {name}: its screen opens here once it is allowed on the phone
peerMenu.ringing: {name} is ringing; it stops when found
peerMenu.removeBody: This machine forgets {name}: its key, its link and, if it was one, its trust as a builder of updates. Shared disks, audio and input with it stop now. {name} keeps calling but is refused; to bring it back, pair the two machines again.
peerMenu.removedHint: Remove this machine on {name} too, or pair again to bring it back.

placement.title: Arrange machines
placement.description: Drag this machine to the cell it sits in. The cursor crosses to whichever machine is next in that direction.
placement.applied: Saved; peers see the new position at once.
placement.pinned: Saved, but --at on the command line overrides it until the node is started without it.
placement.sameCell: Same cell as {names}: machines in one cell border nothing, so the cursor will not cross between them.
placement.unplacedTitle: Not on the grid until they connect
placement.peerNotMine: A peer's place is set on that machine, in its own Cursio app.

pair.title: Pair a machine
pair.description: Show a code on one machine and enter it on the other. The code is used once and never leaves the two machines.
pair.showHint: Then enter it on the other machine in the Cursio app, or run `cursio pair CODE` there.
pair.enterTitle: Enter a code from the other machine
pair.enterHint: The eight characters shown there, with or without the dash.
pair.showThis: Enter this on the other machine
pair.waiting: Code accepted. Waiting for the other machine…
pair.failedAttempts: Wrong code tried {n} time(s); three closes the window.
pair.expired: The code expired before it was used. Show a new one.
pair.tooMany: Too many wrong codes, so pairing was closed. Show a new code.
pair.cliCommands:
cursio pair            # show a code here
cursio pair ABCD-EFGH  # enter one from the other machine
pair.cancelBody: The code stops working at once; the other machine has to start again with a new one.
pair.nearbyHint: A code reaches only the machines listed here.
pair.nobodyTitle: No other Cursio machine is visible
pair.nobodyBody: Nothing on this network can use a code yet. Check that the other machine runs Cursio and is on the same network, not a guest network or a VPN; that a phone's hotspot does not isolate its clients; and that the firewall lets Cursio through.
pair.nobodyCli: Where the network blocks discovery, pair from a terminal by address: cursio mesh --pair --pair-addr ADDRESS:46073

settings.autostartDescription: Off unless you turn it on.
settings.autostartNodeHint: Linux: a systemd user service. Windows: the Run key; the node asks for administrator rights as it does from a terminal.
settings.autostartTrayHint: Starts this app hidden, in the notification area.
settings.autostartFailed: Start at login was not changed
settings.themeDescription: Kept on this machine for this app.
settings.micGateHint: Who records from this machine's microphone on another device hears it only while you speak. Auto follows the mic's background noise.
settings.micGatePinned: A command-line flag fixes the microphone gate; this choice is saved for when the node runs without it.
settings.micGateFailed: The microphone gate was not changed
settings.callsDescription: This computer as a paired phone's Bluetooth headset: the call's voice and the phone's sound come through here.
settings.callsRolesTaken: Cursio is the phones' headset and speaker
settings.callsRolesKept: PipeWire still holds the roles. Run this once, then restart the node:
settings.callsNoPhones: No phone is paired with this computer over Bluetooth.
settings.callsUnpaired: Not paired over Bluetooth: {phones}. Their calls ring here, but the voice stays on the phone until you pair it with this computer in the system's Bluetooth settings.
settings.callsAnswerMoves: Answering here brings the voice here
settings.callsAnswerMovesHint: As on Phone Link: answer or dial from a computer and the call's voice comes to it. Answer on the phone and it stays there.
settings.callsVoiceHint: "Where I am" follows you to the machine this one's mouse is driving.
settings.callsUnsupported: Only a Linux computer can be a phone's Bluetooth headset. Calls still show here, and a call another computer carries can bring its voice to this one.
settings.standbyDescription: When the network stops reaching a paired machine, the connection to it moves to Bluetooth instead of stopping.
settings.bluetoothModeHint: Automatic leaves it off on a machine whose Wi-Fi card is known to lose the network while Bluetooth is busy.
settings.standbyHint: Moves within seconds when Wi-Fi drops, at the cost of a little battery and some Wi-Fi speed on 2.4 GHz. Without it, Bluetooth takes over once Wi-Fi has been gone for 20 seconds. Machines have to be paired over Bluetooth.
settings.standbyFailed: The Bluetooth standby was not changed
settings.restarting: Restarting; peers reconnect in a few seconds.
settings.restartBody: Every link drops for a few seconds and peers' disks unmount while it comes back. Only needed for settings marked as waiting for a restart.
settings.nameDescription: What other machines in the mesh call this one.
settings.nameTooLong: A name is at most {max} characters
settings.renamed: Renamed. Peers see the new name after the node restarts.
settings.renamedPhone: Renamed. Cursio is restarting on this phone so peers see the new name.
settings.namePhoneHint: Renaming restarts Cursio on this phone; its links drop for a few seconds.
settings.nameWaits: Peers still see the old name until the node restarts.

phoneAudio.title: Phone audio → computer
phoneAudio.description: Play what this phone plays on one of your machines' outputs.
phoneAudio.none: No connected machine offers an output device.
phoneAudio.limits: Android lets apps capture media and game sound only from apps that allow it. Calls and notifications are never captured.
phoneAudio.routed: This phone's sound now plays on the computer
phoneAudio.stopped: This phone's sound plays here again
phoneAudio.routeFailed: The phone's sound was not redirected
phoneAudio.listFailed: The output devices could not be read
phoneAudio.awaited: {device} is not connected right now. The sound plays on this phone and goes back to it when it returns.
phoneAudio.remembered: Before Cursio restarted, the sound played on {device}. Android asks again after every restart before it lets the sound go there.
phoneAudio.bluetoothHint: Pair this phone with the computer and pick it as the speaker: every app's sound then plays there through Cursio, with no prompt after a restart. Bluetooth adds about a fifth of a second of delay, fine for music and video; for games the option above is quicker.
phoneAudio.bluetoothFailed: The Bluetooth settings did not open

phoneScreen.title: This screen → computer
phoneScreen.description: Show this phone's screen in a window on a computer you choose, and use it there with the mouse.
phoneScreen.showing: Showing this screen on your computers
phoneScreen.consent: Android asks before anything of the screen leaves the phone.
phoneScreen.noTouch: The computers can see the screen but not touch it: turn on control from a computer above.
phoneScreen.noComputers: No computer is connected to this phone right now.

pad.idle: Choose a machine above to start controlling it
pad.noTargets: No paired machine is connected to this phone. Pair one, or check that it is running.
pad.ready: Slide a finger to move the pointer
pad.hints: Tap to click · Two-finger tap to right-click · Two fingers to scroll or pinch · Three or four to swipe
pad.fullHints: Tap to click · Two-finger tap to right-click · Two fingers to scroll or pinch · Three or four to swipe · Hold a button below and slide to drag
pad.lost: That machine's link is gone; the pad picks it up again when it comes back

screenAsk.title: {computer} wants to show this screen
screenAsk.description: You can see and control this phone from {computer} until you stop it here or close its window there.
